question: How many did God kill for committing whoredom with the daughters of Moab?
summary: Numbers 25:9 puts the death toll from the Baal-Peor plague at 24,000. Paul, citing the same incident in 1 Corinthians 10:8, says 23,000 fell in one day. The numbers don't match.

reconcile.connective: Defenders harmonize the totals by partitioning the dead — Paul counts only those felled by the plague itself, while Moses adds those executed by the judges.

discrepancy.connective: The classic objection comes from Isaac of Troki, who pressed Paul's "twenty-three thousand" as a plain contradiction of Moses' "twenty-four thousand" for the very same Baal-Peor plague.

skeptic.name: Isaac ben Abraham of Troki
skeptic.attribution: Isaac ben Abraham of Troki (d. 1594), Chizzuk Emunah / Faith Strengthened (1593), Part 2, ch. 36; Eng. trans. Moses Mocatta (1851)

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on 1 Corinthians 10:8
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this exact discrepancy at length, arguing Moses counts all the dead (including those hanged) while Paul counts only those who 'fell' by the plague in one day, so the totals agree.

link.title: Numbers 25:9 - Why does this verse say that 24,000 died when 1 Corinthians 10:8 offers a different number?

excerpts.excerpt_text: Only twenty-three thousand perished (Co1 10:8) from pestilence. Moses includes those who died by the execution of the judges [Num 25:5].
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly names both figures (23,000 / 24,000) and reconciles them by distinguishing plague-deaths from judge-executions — the standard harmonization, stated in the fewest verbatim sentences.
